capture.final_message:
Use the model \(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\) for `Real.Angle` and prove the two conjuncts separately.

- Since \(\pi/2\in(-\pi,\pi]\), the canonical representative of `Angle.coe (π / 2)` is \(\pi/2\), giving the first equality.
- `toIocMod (2π) … ψ θ` differs from \(\theta\) by an integral multiple of \(2\pi\). Hence both have the same image in `Real.Angle`, proving the left side of the `Iff`.
- For the right side, represent an angle by \(x=\theta.toReal\in(-\pi,\pi]\). The equation
  \[
  2\theta=\operatorname{coe}(\pi)
  \]
  says \(2x-\pi\in2\pi\mathbb Z\). The bounds on \(x\) leave only \(x=\pi/2\) and \(x=-\pi/2\), yielding exactly the stated disjunction; verify both candidates by computation modulo \(2\pi\).

Thus both propositions joined by the `Iff` are true, so the equivalence follows from their separate proofs.
